jobs.title: Support Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Launching a mobile service requires stitching together carriers, regulations, payments, and support across markets. We’ve built the platform. The next challenge is scaling operations so customers go live smoothly, stay healthy, and their learnings feed back into the product.

You will own the end-to-end support experience across the customer lifecycle, from launch readiness and implementation through post-launch optimization. You will partner closely with customers to design and run their support motion, identify the moments that drive contacts and dissatisfaction, and turn those insights into playbooks and improvements that make every new launch smoother and every user experience better. You will operate with high autonomy and report to the Head of Support.

This role is for someone who thrives in complexity, communicates confidently with senior customer stakeholders, and uses AI as default leverage to move faster and build better.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Be the face of Gigs with customers. Serve as the primary point of contact across pre-sales, implementation, and post-launch. Build the kind of relationships where customers call you first when something goes wrong—because they trust you to fix it.

 - Dig into the data. Track activation funnels, identify drop-off and degradation patterns, run root cause analyses on performance issues. Turn what you find into clear, actionable recommendations—not dashboards that collect dust.

 - Take field insights back to the product. You'll see where the platform breaks in practice before anyone else does. Structure that knowledge and bring it to Product and Engineering in a way they can act on. You're the closest thing to a field reporter we have.

 - Build AI into how you work. Use AI tools to automate recurring tasks, accelerate analysis, prototype lightweight internal tooling, and generally move faster than headcount would otherwise allow. This is a working expectation, not a perk.

 - Know the platform end to end. Get deep into how Gigs works—provisioning, billing, support tooling, connectivity infrastructure. You should be able to explain any part of the system to a customer and diagnose any part of it when it fails.

 - Build what scales. Write the runbooks, design the workflows, and document what you learn so that the next deployment goes faster than the last. What you build should outlast your direct involvement.

 - Keep things moving. Help cross-functional teams stay coordinated and accountable. Unblock what needs unblocking. Reduce friction without creating bureaucracy.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in a demanding operational environment—strategy & operations, bizops, management consulting, technical account management, or somewhere else where you had to figure out how to get hard things done with imperfect information. You've operated under pressure. You know what it feels like to own something that matters.

 - You are self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You don't need someone to hand you a problem definition. You find the problem, form a view on how to solve it, and start moving. We'd rather tell you to slow down than push you to speed up.

 - AI is part of your working stack. You use AI tools daily—for analysis, automation, building internal tooling, accelerating research. You can point to specific things you've built or automated that didn't exist before you made them. This is a working expectation, not a cultural point.

 - You can read the room and the data. Comfortable running SQL, building in spreadsheets, working across BI tools. You can translate a data finding into a business decision and communicate it clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

 - Technically curious. You don't need to be an engineer. But you need to be the kind of person who reads API documentation for fun, asks sharp questions in engineering conversations, and understands enough about how systems work to be dangerous in a good way.

 - Credible with customers. You can run an external meeting with a customer's executive team, manage post-launch relationships with follow-through and care, and represent Gigs in a way that builds trust rather than dependency.

 - High ownership, low ego. You juggle context across multiple workstreams without dropping threads. You take pride in making complex things work reliably, not in getting credit for it. When something is yours, it gets done.

Bonus points if

 - You have experience in telecoms, fintech, or B2B SaaS—especially anything touching connectivity, payments, or platform operations.

 - You've worked in a customer-facing implementation or technical account management role and know what good looks like.

 - You've built or improved internal tooling, reporting infrastructure, or automated workflows using AI or no-code tools.

 

Salary Range: $140,000 - $190,000

jobs.title: Head of Operations
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As Head of Operations you will own 3 areas:

First, the path from signed contract to live revenue. When a partner signs for one of our product lines (Gigs for Work, Connect, API), marketing, implementation, product, partner management, and go-to-market each own a piece of what happens next, and nobody owns the whole thing. Launches take longer than they should. You will own that path end to end and turn it into a process we can repeat.

Second, the company's operating cadence. Gigs is approaching 200 people, and the planning cycles, business reviews, and decision forums need a full-time owner. The founders do this work today, which pulls them away from strategy. You will take it over, and make sure the goals leadership sets reach every team that has to deliver them.

Lastly, you will also run Business Operations, and set the operational standards that our functional ops teams work to. This role sets the pace and the bar for how Gigs operates. You will build what does not exist yet, not maintain what already does.

Compensation: $300K+ and a significant equity package. 


WHAT YOU WILL OWN

1. Customer and partner lifecycle, from signed deal to live revenue

 - Own the process that takes a partner from signed contract to live, revenue-generating product.

 - Build one repeatable launch process with clear stages, named owners, timelines, and go-live readiness criteria, so no launch gets reinvented.

 - Stitch together the handoffs between go-to-market, partner management, implementation, product, and support, and close the gaps where work currently stalls.

 - Shorten time to launch as the playbook matures, and make that number visible to the company.

 - Build the feedback loops, internal and external, that show where launches get stuck.

2. Company operating cadence and business reporting

 - Design and run the rituals that keep Gigs coordinated: annual planning, quarterly goal cycles, leadership syncs, and business reviews.

 - Run a goal-setting framework teams use and trust, and make sure goals travel all the way down, so an engineering manager's team knows what it is building and how it ladders up.

 - Build a single source of truth for company-level KPIs, with a monthly and quarterly business review process that has a consistent format and clear ownership.

 - Run clear decision forums so issues surface early and do not stall.

 - Build the operational layer that catches and routes day-to-day escalations, so founders stop being the default path.

3. Operational standards across functions

 - Operations capability at Gigs sits inside functions: support ops, growth ops, people ops, connectivity ops, and later product, legal, and talent ops. That is healthy. Without a layer above it, each function optimises locally, tooling fragments, and cross-functional dependencies get dropped.

 - Set the shared operating principles, tooling conventions, and process standards that functional ops teams apply in their own domains.
   
   - Keep reporting consistent and non-duplicative across those teams.
   
   - Work with connectivity ops on reliability: clear SLAs, escalation paths, and quality monitoring for provisioning and activation.

 - Over time there is a path for functional ops leads to report into this role, consolidating operational leadership under one owner.

4. Business Operations

 - Own the BizOps team, which covers the work that does not fit inside one function.

 - Expansion operations: the operational backbone for launching new markets and products, working with go-to-market, product, and partnerships so new bets land well.

 - AI operations: Gigs' internal leverage from AI. Find where AI compresses work, pilot the tooling, embed the workflows, and prove the efficiency.

 - Special projects: the high-priority cross-functional projects that sit above any single team, where speed and a dedicated owner matter more than org lines.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You have built operational infrastructure at a high-growth startup or scaleup, ideally through a 250+ person scaling phase. You built it, you did not inherit it.

 - You straddle two layers that rarely sit in one person. You can run real operations (playbooks, process design, launches, ops teams) and you can think strategically about where the business should go. Strong on one and thin on the other will not work here.

 - You have owned a process that crosses many functions and made it hold, including the handoffs, the owners, and the follow-through.

 - Strong planning and process instincts. You can design a planning cycle, run a business review, and build accountability systems without over-engineering them.

 - Analytically sharp. You define the metrics, work with the data, and build the reporting yourself rather than queueing a data team.

 - You set pace. You are direct, you close loops, and you raise the bar for how the people around you work. This is a culture-setting hire.

 - A track record of using AI as a real operational lever, with efficiency you can point to rather than tools you can list.

 - Helpful: exposure to international expansion, market launches, multi-jurisdiction operations, telecom, payments, or API-first infrastructure.

 - Based in or moving to New York or San Francisco.

jobs.title: Business Operations
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As a Business Operations (BizOps) hire, you’ll play a critical role in solving high-impact strategic and operational challenges across the company. You’ll work directly with the founder’s office and leadership team to turn vision into execution, bringing data-driven insights and operational rigor to our most pressing priorities.

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the trajectory of a fast-growing startup by building the BizOps function from the ground up. You’ll operate at the intersection of strategy, operations, finance, and product — a trusted problem-solver and thought partner to teams across the business.

What you will do

 - Partner with the executive team to identify and drive forward high-leverage strategic initiatives across departments (e.g. go-to-market, pricing, international expansion, planning).

 - Build scalable business processes to support rapid growth — from first principles through implementation.

 - Define key metrics, build dashboards, and deliver insights that drive better decisions across the company.

 - Structure and solve ambiguous business problems, distilling complex data into actionable recommendations.

 - Lead cross-functional initiatives and ensure clear communication and accountability across stakeholders.

 - Own strategic planning cadences, including annual planning, quarterly reviews, and operating rhythms.

 - Serve as a force multiplier for the leadership team, helping translate vision into scalable execution.

 - Run toward whatever is most pressing. Jump on the urgent, ambiguous, or unowned problems and drive them to resolution, whatever the function.

 - Use AI to work faster and go deeper: automate analysis, accelerate research, prototype workflows, and build leverage the rest of the team can reuse.

What we are looking for

 - 3-5+ years of experience in a high-performance environment such as management consulting, investment banking, private equity, or in a BizOps / Strategy & Operations / roles at a fast-scaling tech company.

 - Proven track record of tackling unstructured problems and driving initiatives from 0 to 1.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; you’re comfortable modeling in Excel and wrangling data in tools like Looker or SQL.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills — you can drive alignment and clarity across senior stakeholders.

 - Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

 - A collaborative, low-ego mindset and the ability to influence without authority.

 - A genuine curiosity for how things work and a deep desire to make them better.

 - AI fluency. You already use AI tools in your daily work and have sharp instincts for where they add leverage: speeding up analysis, research, drafting, and building repeatable workflows.

 - A bias to run toward problems. You gravitate to the hardest thing in the room and are happy to work on anything that moves the business, regardless of scope or title.

Salary range: $130,000 - $160,000 annually + equity

(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: Growth Strategy and Ops
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Gigs has built a multi-market, multi-product embedded connectivity business, and we're looking for someone to own the operating system the Growth team runs on. This is a high-leverage, cross-functional role sitting at the intersection of strategy, data, and execution, responsible for making the Growth org faster, smarter, and more cohesive.

You will operate with high autonomy and report to the VP of Growth, while working closely with Finance, Legal, and functional leads across GTM, Customer Success, Implementation, and Marketing.

This role is for someone who thrives in complexity, communicates confidently with senior stakeholders, and uses AI as default leverage to move faster and build better.

 

What you will do

 - Own the operating cadence of Growth. Run planning cycles, reporting rhythms, and cross-functional coordination across GTM, Customer Success, Implementation, and Marketing, so Growth runs as one function.

 - Build what lets knowledge travel. Write the playbooks, runbooks, and documentation that take what works in one region and make it work everywhere else. What you build should outlast your direct involvement.

 - Own the data and reporting infrastructure. Build the systems that tell the Growth team what's working and where to focus next.

 - Lead the AI and tooling stack. Make sure the team is actually using AI to multiply output.

 - Drive strategic projects end-to-end. Market expansion, segmentation, GTM playbooks, from framing the problem to shipping the output.

 - Keep the function moving. Unblock what needs unblocking across a multi-market, multi-product Growth team that's operating faster than its infrastructure can handle.

 

What we are looking for

 - 4+ years in a demanding operational environment — biz ops, strategy & ops, management consulting, or growth ops at a fast-scaling company. You've operated under pressure and know what it feels like to own something that matters

 - You are self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You don't need someone to hand you a problem definition. You find the problem, form a view, and start moving. We'd rather tell you to slow down than push you to speed up

 - AI is part of your working stack. You use AI tools daily—for analysis, automation, building internal tooling, accelerating research. You can point to specific things you've built or automated that didn't exist before you made them.

 - You can read the room and the data. You can translate a data finding into a business decision and communicate it clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

 - You're a generalist who goes deep. Comfortable moving between a data problem, a process problem, and a strategic framing problem in the same week.

 - High ownership, low ego. You juggle context across multiple workstreams without dropping threads. You take pride in making complex things work reliably, not in getting credit for it. When something is yours, it gets done.

Bonus points if

 -   You have experience in telecoms, fintech, or B2B SaaS - especially anything touching connectivity or payments. 

 -   You've built or improved internal tooling or automated workflows using AI or no-code tools.

 -   You've operated across multiple markets or regions and know what it takes to make something work globally, not just in one office.

Salary Range: £85,000 - £110,000
(The final offer depends on your background, skills, and how you perform through the process. We're open to considering outlier candidates, which may result in an adjustment to the scope and compensation)

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

As Chief of Staff to the CEO, you are our CEO's force multiplier. You make the CEO and the company move faster and decide better.

You work at the center of Gigs: strategy, the leadership team's operating cadence, board and investor work, and the highest-priority projects in the company. You take first cuts on ambiguous problems, turn rough direction into sharp narratives, and build the mechanisms that keep a fast-scaling company aligned as it grows. When something matters and has no owner, you own it.

This is a senior role. You will sit in rooms with the leadership team, the board, and investors, and you will be trusted to act on the CEO's behalf. It is also a role of high leverage and low ego: your job is to make other people's output better, often without your name on it.

Salary range: $270K - $300K


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Be the CEO's thought partner. Take structured first cuts on the hardest questions. Synthesize context, run the analysis, frame the options and trade-offs, and recommend a path. Give our CEO a sharper starting point than a blank page.

 - Build and run the founders' transmission layer. Turn the founders' priorities into execution across the company. Capture decisions, drive follow-ups, close loops, and make sure nothing important waits on them. This is the operational spine of the founders' office, and you own it.

 - Own board and investor work. Build board decks and investor materials that tell a clear, honest story. Shape the fundraising narrative and the numbers behind it. Prepare the founders for every board meeting and investor conversation so they walk in ready.

 - Write in the founders' voice. Turn rough storylines into polished decks and memos for all-hands, builder meetings, leadership reviews, and external moments.

 - Lead special projects end to end. Take on the urgent, cross-functional, often confidential work: fundraising, org design, new market entry, key hires, the occasional fire. Drive them to done.

 - Act as proxy. Represent the founders in meetings when they can't be there. Carry decisions, unblock teams, and be a reliable channel between the founders and the company.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Senior generalist track record. 8+ years across strategy consulting, banking, VC, or senior strategy/ops roles in high-growth tech. You have run workstreams, teams, or functions, and people trust your judgment.

 - Executive-grade communication. Writing and slides that tell a clear story and drive a decision. You can brief a board and rally a room of builders with the same material.

 - Sound judgment under ambiguity. You make progress with imperfect information and competing priorities. You make the call and own it.

 - Business and financial fluency. You are comfortable with a model, a cap table, a board narrative, and the metrics that run the business. You can hold your own with Finance and investors.

 - High ownership and discretion. Deadline-driven, detail-obsessed, able to run many workstreams without dropping balls. Trusted with the company's most sensitive information.
